sections.heading: Look First, Then Tell You Straight
body: A heating and cooling system rarely fails all at once. Most calls start with one worn part: a capacitor, a relay, a fan motor, a sensor.
That matters, because a small part is a small repair. Before anyone talks about replacing a system, we find out what actually failed.
Then we tell you what it will cost to fix it and, if the system is old enough that replacing it is worth a look, what that would cost too. You decide with both numbers in front of you.
You pay for the work that was done, and nothing that wasn't.

sections.heading: AC Repair
body: The outside unit is running, but the house won't cool. Or it cools for an hour and quits. Or the fan has stopped and the air coming out of the vents is warm.
In Wichita summers, the AC runs most of the day for months. Capacitors, contactors and fan motors wear out under that load, and a part that costs little can take the whole system down.
We find the part that failed, replace it and get the system running again. If the real trouble is bigger, we say so before we do anything.

sections.heading: Furnace Repair
body: A cold house in January is not something to wait on. A furnace that won't light or won't stay on is usually a failed ignitor, a dirty flame sensor, a worn blower motor or a clogged filter.
Many of those are quick fixes, and we'll show you what we found so you know what you're paying for.
A furnace that's failing because of its age is a different conversation, and we'll have that one with you honestly too.

sections.heading: AC and Furnace Replacement
body: Some systems are finished. A furnace that's 30 years old, an AC that has been repaired twice in two summers, a unit running an older refrigerant that's getting harder and more expensive to service.

Replacing the whole system is a big decision, so we don't push it. We explain what you have, what the options are and what size system your house needs, because a unit that's too big or too small never runs right.
Many full system replacements are finished in one day. Before the crew leaves, ask anything you want about the new system and thermostat.

sections.heading: Seasonal Checkups
body: Most people don't think about their system until it fails, usually on the hottest or coldest day of the year.

Dirt, loose wiring and worn parts show up before a breakdown, if someone is looking. A checkup before the cooling season, and another before the heating season, finds them while they're still cheap to fix.
We'll also show you what you can do yourself between visits, like changing the filter and keeping the outdoor unit clear.

sections.heading: Ductwork
body: The ducts are the part of the system you never see, until a remodel opens a wall. A main supply duct that's damaged, undersized or poorly connected leaves rooms too hot or too cold, no matter how good the equipment is.
We replace ductwork, including the main supply duct, and make sure it fits what your system actually needs.

sections.heading: When the AC Runs but the House Won't Cool
body: You walk by the outside unit and it's humming, or the fan isn't spinning at all. Inside, the air from the vents is warm, or it's cool for a while and then it isn't.
Those are the usual signs of a failed part. Wichita summers keep an AC running hard for months, and the parts that start and run the motors wear out first.

The capacitor gives the compressor and fan motors the jolt they need to start. A relay or contactor switches them on. When either one fails, the unit may hum without starting, or not run at all, even though the rest of the system is fine.
Fan motors seize. Drains clog and shut the system down. Dirty coils and filters choke the airflow until the evaporator freezes into a block of ice.
Most of these are repairs, not replacements.

sections.heading: What We Do When We Come Out
body: We start by finding out why it stopped, not by guessing. We check the thermostat, the power, the capacitor, the contactor and relay, the fan motors, the coils, the airflow and the drain.
Once we know what failed, we tell you in plain words what it is and what the repair costs. You get the cost before we replace anything.
Then we replace the part and check that the system is running.

sections.heading: Repair or Replace: What We'll Tell You
body: Age matters more than anything else. An AC usually lasts 12 to 15 years, and one that's older than that, and breaking down every summer, may not be worth another repair.
Refrigerant matters too. Systems built to run R-22 refrigerant, which is no longer made, get more expensive to service every year, so a major repair on one is a harder choice.

If the repair is small and the system is sound, we repair it. If a replacement is coming, we tell you roughly when and what the options are, so you can plan for it instead of being surprised on the hottest day.

sections.heading: Check These Before You Call
body: A few things take two minutes and sometimes solve it.
list: Check that the thermostat is set to cool and the temperature is below the room temperature.
Check that the breaker for the AC hasn't tripped.
Replace a clogged filter. A filter that's full of dust can freeze the coil.
Make sure the outside unit isn't buried in leaves, grass clippings or a fence's worth of weeds.
tail: If the unit is covered in ice, turn the AC off and let it thaw before you call, so the ice doesn't keep damaging the system.
If none of it helps, call us.

sections.heading: Knowing What's Wrong, and What It Costs
body: When something is wrong, you should know what it is.

We walk you through the problem and the choices, and we say honestly if a choice isn't worth it. If a new system is the better answer, we'll help you size and plan the replacement, and we can install it.
A new outside unit also has to sit level and stable. One that settles and tilts puts strain on the compressor and the refrigerant lines, and wears out sooner.

sections.quote: My upstairs AC was failing to blow any air at all, as the outside unit continued to run. I called Mike late in the day. He advised me what to do and he and Austin were out to look at my unit the next afternoon. … The problem was diagnosed and options for a fix were given to me as well as cost. I opted for a new install given the age of my system. The next day, they were prompt and on time. No hidden costs. They went over and beyond to raise and level out my new outside unit!

sections.heading: When the House Is Cold and the Furnace Isn't Working
body: The thermostat is calling for heat and nothing happens. Or the furnace clicks, runs for a minute and shuts off. Or the blower runs and the air coming out is cold.
It feels like the whole system has died, but a furnace has a short list of parts that cause most no-heat calls.
The ignitor lights the burner, and ignitors crack with age.

The flame sensor tells the furnace the burner is lit, and when it gets coated with soot, the furnace shuts the gas off as a safety step. A worn blower motor or a clogged filter keeps the heat from reaching the house, and can make the furnace overheat and shut itself down.
Each of those is a repair, and most of them are small ones.

sections.heading: Helping Us Come Prepared
body: The first call matters. If you can tell us what the furnace is doing, how old it is and what the nameplate on the unit says, give us those details when you phone.
Ignitors, sensors and blower motors differ from one furnace model to the next. Knowing the model before we arrive lets us think through the likely causes and bring parts that fit.
When we get there, we find out what failed, tell you what it is in plain words and tell you what the repair costs before we start. You pay for the work that was done.

sections.quote: Austin was very helpful when our heater wasn’t functioning properly. He talked through what might be the possible issues and requested the information of our unit ahead of time so he could show up prepared with all the parts he would need. sections.heading: Check These Before You Call
body: Two minutes can save you a trip.
list: Make sure the thermostat is set to heat and the temperature is above the room temperature. Replace the batteries if it has them.
Check the furnace's power switch, which looks like a light switch on or near the furnace, and the breaker.
Replace a clogged filter. A furnace that can't pull in air will overheat and shut down.
Make sure the vents in the house are open and nothing is blocking them.
tail: If you smell gas, leave the house and call the gas company from outside. Don't try to relight anything.
If none of it helps, call us.

sections.heading: Repair or Replace
body: A furnace usually lasts 15 to 20 years, sometimes more. When it's older than that, or it needs a major part, the repair bill can be money better put toward a new system.
If your furnace is in good shape and the problem is small, we repair it.
If it's failing, we show you what's wrong, what a replacement involves and what size your home needs. A furnace that's too big short-cycles. One that's too small can't keep up in January.
We don't push a new system. We give you the cost of the repair and the cost of the replacement, and you decide.

sections.quote: When I needed to replace my 30 year old furnace, I called 1st Call Heating and Cooling. They were quick to schedule an appointment and their estimate was very fair. The staff was extremely helpful in explaining the different types of units available and the size needed for my home.

sections.heading: Replacing a Furnace, and the Whole System
body: A furnace and an AC share the same ductwork and blower, and they're often the same age. If both are near the end, replacing them together can be one job instead of two.

We replace furnaces on their own and full heating and cooling systems, and many full systems are installed in a single day. A replacement also means looking at what's around the furnace, like the gas line and venting, and anything wrong there is worth knowing about.

sections.quote: I finally decided to do a full upgrade on a nearly 40 year old furnace and AC system in my house. … Mike and Austin were helpful and prompt in answering any questions I've had and also alerted me to an issue with the gas company's equipment I hadn't been aware of before.
